_README: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for what a packaged SSBM Nucleus build is allowed to
contain. Windows (build.bat), Linux (build-linux.sh), macOS (build-macos.sh)
and the PyInstaller spec (mex_backend.spec) all read THIS file through
tools/build/ship_guard.py. Nothing else may hard-code a copy of these
rules -- that divergence is exactly how the Linux AppImage ended up shipping
5.6 MB of retail costume DATs that the Windows installer had been stripping
for months.
Three sections do the work:
stage[]   -- what gets copied into the disposable packaging stage.
electron-builder runs from the stage, never from the repo,
so the working tree can never leak into an installer.
scrub[]   -- what is then deleted FROM THE STAGE. Never touches the repo.
detect[]  -- what the guard looks for afterwards, by severity.
The app is bring-your-own-ISO: vanilla character/stage/audio data is
extracted from the USER's own ISO at first run and must never ship.
See memory shipped-vanilla-asset-leak.
kind: file|dir. optional=true means 'skip silently if absent'; anything
else is a hard error. Paths are relative to the project root (src) and to
the stage (dst), always with forward slashes.
This list is deliberately per-platform where electron-builder's config is
per-platform. It reproduces each platform's CURRENT payload; it is not an
attempt to make the three installers contain identical files.

common.why: npm ci recreates the exact production dependency tree in the disposable stage.
MIT/Ms-PL/Apache/Zlib notices must reach the end user (Settings > Credits).
Production source maps are debugging artifacts and are not shipped.
Hand-authored Sheik portraits (vanilla Melee has none). DATs are scrubbed below.
Writable CSP recipe tree used by first-run ISO extraction. Processor Python modules are already embedded in mex_backend.

Staged on every platform when the assistant gate ships (by default since 0.9.0): rigswap's own package, compiled at the pinned commit (python tools/build/fetch_rigswap.py, utility/rigswap.manifest.json; the tree is git-ignored). Randall's model import runs it as a subprocess on the tools the user downloads from Settings (Blender 4 and a CPython 3.13 with rigswap's wheels: utility/model_import_tools.json, docs/dev/MODEL_IMPORT_TOOLS.md). Since 0.9.0 neither Blender nor that Python ships in any installer; macOS and Linux shipped no rigswap at all before.

What the app downloads for model import on this platform, each file by URL, sha256 and size from the official sources (backend/randall/model_import/tools). Generated by tools/build/pin_model_import_tools.py.

win.why: Bundled UnRAR for .rar imports. extraResources copies it from the STAGE, so it must be here or .rar archives are refused in the installed app.

Pinned GPL ffmpeg 9.0.2, BtbN FFmpeg-Builds (unmodified, run as a separate process; its Corresponding Source is published beside it, see THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md). Tracker game recordings encode to a compressed mp4 with sound through it; without it a fresh PC saves a huge silent raw AVI. The tree is git-ignored -- reproduce it with `python tools/build/fetch_ffmpeg.py`, which verifies the sha256 in utility/ffmpeg.manifest.json. extraResources copies it from the STAGE, so it must be here or the installed app has no ffmpeg.

linux.why: Bundled UnRAR for .rar imports. extraResources copies it from the STAGE, so it must be here or .rar archives are refused in the installed app.

mac.why: Bundled UnRAR for .rar imports. extraResources copies it from the STAGE, so it must be here or .rar archives are refused in the installed app.

The hardened-runtime entitlements for mac signing. build-macos.sh passes this staged copy to electron-builder as an absolute path, because codesign resolves a relative mac.entitlements against the shell's cwd (app/), not --projectDir. Missing = unsigned/rejected hardened runtime.

scrub.why: A dev checkout's CSP recipe tree can also hold a loose vanilla roster, trophy DATs and CSP_2.zip. Nothing in the app reads them: generate_csp takes its vanilla DATs from the reference bank first-run setup copies out of the user's own ISO into the data folder (storage/test-base/files). Since 0.9.0 setup no longer writes any into the shipped csp_data.

csp_data/<char>/DEFAULT.png, stock.png, csp_Pl*.png and css_icon.png are retail CSPs, CSS icons and stock icons at exact retail dimensions -- straight rips, extracted by a dev years ago and committed. Nothing in the shipped app reads them: the live portrait/stock path is backend/shared/rendering (costume_assets.generate_stock over VANILLA_ASSETS_DIR, itself populated by first_run_setup._copy_character_assets from the user's ISO), and generate_csp only ever reads .anim/.yml out of these folders. The only readers are processor/generate_stock_icon.py's find_stock_template/find_default_csp, reachable solely from that script's own command line -- dev tooling the backend never imports and the installer never ships. Kept in the private repo for that tooling; deleted from every packaged build. Sheik's utility/assets/vanilla PNGs are a separate, hand-authored tree and are NOT touched by this rule.

CostumeValidator/bin/*.bin and the obsolete Windows validator are private test oracles, never runtime payload. The Python validator derives references from the USER's own disc. Keep this defense for any future platform publish tree that accidentally gathers the oracle.

Developer-only: the CSP golden-image regression suite carries 11 full retail costume DATs as fixtures, and the standalone CSP Maker _build output gathers vanilla fighter DATs. Neither is reachable from the app.
Sheik's hand-authored PNG portraits ship; the ISO-extracted DAT/USD files beside them do not.
Debug symbols, logs and interpreter caches are build-machine leftovers, not runtime payload.
scrub._keep_why: rigswap's package ships as bytecode only (tools/build/fetch_rigswap.py compiles it and deletes the source), so these .pyc files are the model importer itself, not an interpreter cache.

verify._README: Paths (relative to the stage) that MUST exist after staging, or the installer would be silently broken. Mirrors build.bat's 'Verifying critical bundle artifacts' block.

_README: Trees that mex_backend.spec bundles INSIDE the PyInstaller onefile exe.
They never appear as loose files in the stage, so the stage scan cannot
see them -- the guard scans them straight from the project root and
labels them 'inside mex_backend'. Keep in step with the spec's datas[].

roots.exclude_why: The spec walks backend/assets file by file and skips whatever ship_guard.detect_excluded('retail-hud-and-pause', rel) matches -- these globs ARE that category's paths. Since 2026-11-19 the source tree no longer holds these PNGs at all (the readers use only the copy derived from the user's own game); the exclude and the spec's skip stay so a re-added picture still cannot reach the exe. Keep the two in step, and never add an exclude for a tree that really does ship: this is the one place the guard trusts the spec instead of looking.

roots.include_why: The spec does NOT bundle backend/data wholesale -- it names these files one by one (mex_backend.spec's expected_backend_data tuple), so they are the entire embedded tree. Without the include the guard reports source-only leftovers such as backend/data/__pycache__/*.pyc as being inside mex_backend, which Analysis-00.toc/PKG-00.toc show they are not. Add a path here when, and only when, the spec starts embedding it. menus/compatibility_manifest.json joined the spec's tuple and this list on 2026-09-22; tests/backend/test_ship_guard_embedded_roots.py compares the two and had been red since the spec moved first.

_README: severity BLOCK  -- always fails the build. Every BLOCK category is fully
handled by a scrub rule above, so a correct build never
trips one. A BLOCK hit means the scrub rules and the
tree have drifted apart: fix the tree or the rule.
severity REVIEW -- retail-derived content that is (or may be) load-bearing
and whose fate is the owner's call. Fails the build
unless NUCLEUS_ALLOW_UNRESOLVED_ASSETS=1 is set, which
prints a loud banner and marks the build unpublishable.
severity NOTE   -- never fails. Reported so the inventory is honest
(bloat, dev leftovers).
'paths' are globs against the stage-relative path (** = any depth,
* does not cross /); 'names' are globs against the basename; 'exts' are
file extensions. Matching is case-insensitive. 'except_names' /
'except_paths' exempt specific files and MUST carry an honest reason.

categories.title: Retail fighter / trophy model data
categories.why: Pl*/Ty* DAT+USD files are verbatim Melee game data. first_run_setup repopulates them from the user's own ISO.

categories.title: Retail archives, discs and sound banks
categories.why: Whole-ISO, DOL and SSM payloads, plus the CSP_2.zip roster archive.

categories.title: Ripped Melee menu audio
categories.why: main.ssm indices 115-216. first_run_setup._extract_menu_sounds re-extracts them from the user's ISO via HSDRawViewer --sound extract.

categories.title: Developer-only trees carrying retail fixtures
categories.why: csp_regression/cases holds 11 full retail costume DATs (~5.6 MB); processor/_build gathers vanilla fighter DATs into the standalone CSP Maker. Users never reach either.

categories.title: Unreleased-feature media
categories.why: Project policy: nothing unreleased ships, reachable OR present. The in-app promo/trailer videos were deleted (the gates are now a plain Patreon button); this keeps the whole promo tree out of the payload so a re-added trailer for a gated feature -- Randall/the Analyst -- cannot ship again.

categories.title: Select-screen backdrops (CSS / SSS layout editors)
categories.why: FIXED 2026-11-19 (owner's rule: nothing that can be made from the game ships in the desktop app). css_template.png / sss_template.png were 640x527 screenshots of the running game that the CSS and SSS layout editors drew icons on; they are DELETED. HSDLib v2026.11.19.1 added HSDRawViewer --menu-render, which draws MnSlChr / MnSlMap through the camera, lights and fog the file defines, posed at the screen's idle state (four closed doors and no icons on the CSS; frame and background on the SSS). backend/shared/vanilla_extract/menu_backdrops.py renders both from the vanilla MnSlChr.usd / MnSlMap.usd taken out of the user's own ISO into utility/assets/menu_refs/menu_backdrops (on demand at /api/mex/menus/{css,sss}/backdrop, and warmed at app start); without an ISO or a renderer the editors draw a plain panel. The only differences from the old screenshots are run-time text (the rules banner) and slight shading. BLOCK so a re-added screenshot fails the build.

categories.title: Ripped CSS portraits (MnSlChr*)
categories.why: MnSlChr* is the retail select-screen file and the CSS portraits ripped from it. None is tracked in git; the copies a csp_data tree can gather are scrubbed (scrub rule csp-data-roster). NOTE so one that turns up in another tree is listed. The layout editors' backdrops, which used to share this rule, are rule retail-menu-backdrops.

categories.title: In-game effect frames (Extras pictograms)
categories.why: STILL MELEE-DERIVED, ACCEPTED (owner decision 2026-08-19). 84 crops of in-game harness captures: the recolour in each is ours, the render underneath is Melee's, and some frames include characters and stages (common_fire_color1 is Zelda). They are NOT original art and this rule must not be reworded to say so. Kept because no extraction path exists at any price -- they are screenshots of the running game, not files on the disc. Disposition is REPLACE or keep, never EXTRACT. NOTE so a release build can go green without NUCLEUS_ALLOW_UNRESOLVED_ASSETS.

categories.title: Retail animation slices in csp_data
categories.why: Sheik IntroL/IntroR/NeutralB and Young Link Wait were byte-exact slices of retail animation data. They were DELETED in 31fdbd2; this rule now stands as the tripwire that catches another one. The Pl*/Ty* naming rule never matched them -- that gap is why they shipped. .anim was deliberately REMOVED from this rule on 2026-08-19: those are Maya ASCII pose exports (animVersion 1.1 / mayaVersion 2018), a format that cannot be byte-derived from the disc, and the owner confirms they are hand-authored CSP poses. They are also load-bearing -- generate_csp picks one per character as the pose source, so deleting them breaks portraits for a dozen fighters.

categories.title: Per-bone transform tables extracted from retail Pl*.dat
categories.why: FIXED 2026-08-19. CostumeValidator/bin/*_Share_joint.bin is 159 skeleton tables lifted out of retail costume files. They no longer ship: utility/tools/processor/bone_tables.py writes the same records and backend/shared/vanilla_extract/bone_refs.py derives them from the USER's disc -- each costume DAT read at its FST offset, ~1s for the lot -- into <storage>/test-base/bone-refs. first_run_setup Phase 4b does it at setup, and core.config registers a provider so an install that predates that generates them the first time a costume is validated (a validator with no references silently reports EVERY costume netplay-safe, which is what shipped in 0.6.4). Derivation is byte-exact against all 159 -- tests/backend/test_bone_tables.py asserts it, because the validator copies these transforms verbatim into people's costumes. mex_backend.spec no longer embeds bin/ and the bone-reference-tables scrub rule strips it from the electron stage; the in-tree copies stay in the private repo as that test's oracle. REVIEW rather than NOTE now that the derivation exists: the glob stays wide on purpose so a re-added copy trips the guard.

categories.title: Vanilla portraits, stock icons and CSS icons
categories.why: Retail CSPs/stocks at exact retail dimensions. NONE of them ship any more: per-costume csp.png/stock.png come from first_run_setup._copy_character_assets out of the user's own ISO into PROJECT_ROOT (the writable dir config.VANILLA_ASSETS_DIR points at), and the csp_data DEFAULT/stock/csp_Pl*/css_icon rips are stripped from both the electron stage and the mex_backend embed by the csp-data-portraits scrub rule. The globs stay wide on purpose so a re-added rip trips the guard; the only exemption is Sheik, below.
categories._except_why: Sheik: vanilla Melee has no separate Sheik portraits, so there is nothing in an ISO to extract and these PNGs are hand-authored artwork, not retail data -- that is exactly why first_run_setup.PRESERVE_CSP_CHARACTERS skips Sheik and _copy_bundled_sheik_assets stages them in Phase 0. Owner-accepted, docs/dev/VANILLA_ASSET_POLICY.md sec.2. The exemption is Sheik ONLY: any other character folder appearing under utility/assets/vanilla still trips this category. Note the stage manifest copies just utility/assets/vanilla/Sheik, so no other folder can reach a build through that route either. Separately, the vanilla/ tree collects render debug logs and CSP recipe YAML; those are build leftovers, not artwork, and fall through to build-leftovers instead of inflating this category.

categories.title: Stage select-screen art
categories.why: FIXED 2026-11-19 (owner's rule: nothing that can be made from the game ships in the desktop app). Neither half ships. The six tourney PNGs under utility/assets/stages come from first_run_setup Phase 3. The stage-select icon and banner of every versus stage -- the old backend/assets/vanilla_stages, which rode inside the backend exe for Tracker's stage icons -- are copied out of the user's own m-ex project (data/stages/<internal id>.json -> assets/sss/*.png, byte-identical to the 46 files that used to ship) by backend/shared/vanilla_extract/menu_refs.py into utility/assets/menu_refs/vanilla_stages, at first-run setup (Phase 4c) and on project open while missing. Tracker's stage icons, the stage-slot panel and vanilla stage imports read only that copy. The phone and website are separate builds and are no reason to bundle them here. BLOCK so a re-added copy fails the build.

categories.title: HUD glyphs, pause-screen textures and series emblems
categories.why: FIXED 2026-08-19 (the imagery). The GmPause textures, the IfAll glyph and word-banner previews and the m-ex series emblems are retail pictures, and the app already ships the tool that makes them. backend/shared/vanilla_extract/menu_refs.py exports them on the user's machine into utility/assets/menu_refs -- HSDRawViewer --pause-screen export on GmPause, --hud-textures export on both IfAll regions, and a copy out of the project's own assets/series/ -- in ~3.8s, byte-identical to the copies that used to ship (tests/backend/test_menu_refs.py). first_run_setup Phase 4c derives them and core.state.set_project_path derives whatever is missing on project open, so existing installs self-heal. The tracked copies and the bundled fallback were DELETED 2026-11-19 (pause_vanilla/manifest.json with its textures, since it only names them): the editors read the derived copy and report the art missing until it exists. Source MUST be a mexcli project, not the raw disc: m-ex adds an Eblm_matanim_joint root, so a project's IfAll export has 1349 slots where the disc's has 1333, and percent._build_replacement_spec injects against GLOBAL indices in the project's file. DELIBERATELY NOT LISTED: hud_vanilla/manifest_{usd,dat}.json and pause_vanilla/manifest.json -- dimensions, formats and a raw-buffer md5 per slot, i.e. fingerprints and coordinates rather than imagery, the same call as backend/assets/texture_regions. They stay bundled on purpose so the install path -- the one that can mis-map a mod into the wrong IfAll slots -- never depends on runtime derivation. Only the .png globs are enforced, at BLOCK so a re-added picture fails the build.

categories.title: Plain DAS loaders (the game's own stage files, patched)
categories.why: FIXED 2026-11-19. No DAS loader ships as a file. GrPs.usd, the Pokemon Stadium loader, carried the transformation models (81% of its 32-byte blocks occur verbatim in the vanilla GrPs.usd); the other five kept 13-73% of their vanilla roots (GrIz 73%, GrSt 70% plus Shy Guy's shape-animation joint, GrNLa 49%, GrOp 17%, GrNBa 13%). Each ships as <root>.xdelta in utility/DynamicAlternateStages (6-8 KB each, plain VCDIFF, no secondary compression; no 32-byte block of any patch occurs in its vanilla root) and is rebuilt from the user's own vanilla NTSC 1.02 root at DAS install time with the xdelta3 the app already ships for patches (projects/install/das_loaders.py; source and result are both SHA-256 checked, and the result is cached in utility/assets/das_loaders). BLOCK so a plain loader cannot come back beside its patch. (The id keeps its first name; it now covers all six.)

categories.title: Dynamic Alternate Stages payloads
categories.why: ACCEPTED (owner's call 2026-11-19). Only the six xdelta patches ship here (GrIz, GrNBa, GrNLa, GrOp, GrSt .dat.xdelta and GrPs.usd.xdelta): only what DAS changed, applied to the user's own vanilla root at install (projects/install/das_loaders.py). The plain loaders are BLOCKed by das-stadium-loader. NOTE so a release build can go green without the override.

categories.title: Build/run leftovers
categories.why: Caches and logs that add weight and can carry local paths.
categories._except_why: rigswap's compiled package: its .pyc files are the shipped code (scrub rule build-leftovers keeps them).

_README: Regexes run over the frozen backend exe read as latin1. PyInstaller's
archive TOC stores every embedded data file's path as a literal string,
so embedded retail data is detectable as text. Path-shaped only -- a
match is a strong signal, not proof, so these are reported at REVIEW
unless listed in 'block'.
2026-08-19: these patterns match PATHS, so a directory-prefix rule fires on
every file under it. The old hud_vanilla/pause_vanilla/vanilla_stages rule
did exactly that and blocked the first real macOS build. Verified against
that build's ship-report: hud_vanilla/ and pause_vanilla/ now contribute
ONLY the bare directory string -- their imagery is derived from the user's
own game at first run -- but the JSON manifests kept there on purpose
(dimensions/formats/md5s: fingerprints, not imagery) still put the prefix
in the TOC. So that rule now matches image FILES. 2026-11-19: the HUD,
pause, series and vanilla_stages pictures are all derived from the user's
own game and deleted from the tree, so an image file under any of those
four directories in the exe is a BLOCK (only the HUD slot manifests, which
are JSON, still put the hud_vanilla prefix in the TOC).
